pending_commit.commit_message: factory: dict.keys() in py2 change to list(dict) In python2, dict.keys() return a copy list of keys. In python3, dict.keys() return an iterator of keys. The semantic changes, so we need to use list(dict) to get a copy list. BUG=chromium:999876 TEST=make test Change-Id: Ic719a5cf08d448241d9f631fcb36103e73940a6b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1824719 Tested-by: Yilin Yang <kerker@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yong Hong <yhong@chromium.org>

factory: Use six.reraise to raise error with traceback python2 only: raise Error, "value", traceback python3 only: raise Error("value").with_traceback() Hence we need to import reraise from six package to reach a compatible state. Import it as "raise_", because this is the name in future.utils. Note: from `future.utils import raise_` is another way, but in dut, there is no module called future. BUG=chromium:999876 TEST=make test Change-Id: Ie4827bf61038a16e2e71c98f8cd8583966e30d0e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1832959 Tested-by: Yilin Yang <kerker@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yong Hong <yhong@chromium.org>

This is because the CTS Instant doesn't support --include-filter option. This CL changes the rule to unify the logics: - For the test with one module: use --moduel option - For the test with multiple modules: use --include-filter option This rule is ok since the CTS instant only has the tests with one module.
